channel.title: Federal News Network - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Federal News Network (federalnewsnetwork.com)

item.title: Maryland’s new data tool illuminates local impact of federal decisions
item.description: "We wanted to give our partners a tool to understand: How will these cuts affect the state, but especially, how will they affect the county?" Ben Siegel said.

item.title: VHA saw the highest uptick in law enforcement staffing from 2020-2024, GAO finds
item.description: GAO’s report doesn’t cover the last year when the Department of Homeland Security recruited a record number of immigration enforcement and Border Patrol agents.

item.title: Fraudulent research is costing taxpayers millions and undermining scientific integrity
item.description: By exploiting weaknesses in affiliations, citations and publication credibility, bad actors in research are securing federal grants.

item.title: How the FAA built the first zero trust network — long before cybersecurity existed
item.description: Don Parente, a vice president at MetTel, explains why the air traffic control system is a great example of putting the “trust, but verify” adage into practice.

item.title: Marco Rubio out as acting head of National Archives
item.description: Before the end of his tenure, Rubio tapped James Byron, senior advisor to the archivist, to serve and perform the functions of archivist.

item.title: Five updates on the Trump admin’s cybersecurity agenda
item.description: From a new national cyber strategy to highly anticipated actions around AI security, here are five things worth watching on the cyber policy front.

item.title: Leaders face a common challenge in understanding emerging backbone of power
item.description: "Policymakers and implementers speak a different language than engineers," Michelle Giuda said. "We want to educate at scale in order to meet the moment."

item.title: Lawmakers cap NGC2 funding, Army warns industry not to ‘bring negativity’ to Congress
item.description: "We have seen vendors bring negativity and interactions on Capitol Hill. I'll be clear: for the Army, it's a non-starter,” Michael Obadal said.

item.title: Lawmakers form new caucus to advocate for federal workforce reforms
item.description: The launch of the bicameral Federal Workforce Caucus comes after a year of major changes to the career civil service under the Trump administration.

item.title: Are federal programs doing enough to prevent fraud?
item.description: "We're really developing the risk tolerance. There is always going to be a certain amount of fraud or improper payments in any program," Hannah Padilla said.
